# Tutorials — road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: in progress. The owner's answers (2026-10-31) are in §10; TU0
records the decisions in spec §11.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model tutorials** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Tutorials are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The tutorial dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Tutorials get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Tutorial**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project or
the practice project. It is the word in the menu (Help ▸ Tutorials) and in
the code. The word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: walkthrough,
wizard (which suggests the app makes the choices), lesson.

**Practice project**: a small project bundled with the app, with media made
for the tutorials, that Help ▸ Tutorials opens as an untitled copy so the
bundled one is never written (§5a).

**Step**: one numbered item in a tutorial. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
Me does.

## 4. The shape

### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list

A tutorial is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Tutorial:`
heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

```markdown
### Tutorial: change a clip's volume
<!-- tutorial {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
```

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every tutorial into one `Tutorials.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

### 4.2 The step vocabulary

**The normative text is spec §11 TU-2** (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`); this
section is the first draft. TU1 added `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a
menu form of Show Me, `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the
filter's `follows_clip` and `has_transition`.

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.
Every key is optional except that a step has a sentence.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the tutorial does not require this step. |

Variables: `$selection` (the clip ids when the step began), `$created`
(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip
in time order that matches, for a Show Me that has to choose a clip).

### 4.3 The runner and the coach panel

- **The coach panel.** A small non-activating floating panel beside the
  editor window, the same kind of panel as the recorder. It shows the title,
  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.
- **The spotlight.** A borderless, click-through child window over the
  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when
  the layout moves. Because it is a window, it sits above the Metal and
  `AVPlayerLayer` layers.
- **Needs.** Before step 1, the tutorial's `needs` are checked against the
  open project. When they are not met, the panel says what is missing and
  how to get it, and offers the practice project (§5a), for example "This
  tutorial needs a clip with sound. Open the practice project, or open a
  movie of your own (File ▸ Open…)". It does not start until they are met.
- **Where to start one.** **Help ▸ Tutorials ▸** has one submenu per guide
  page, filled from `Tutorials.json`. A "Try it in Frame Job" link from
  the online guide (`framejob://tutorial/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

### 4.4 Show Me

Show Me's tool form (and each tool entry of a list) runs through
`AgentServer.execute`, the path the Assistant's calls take; its menu form
performs the built menu bar's own item, the path a click takes, with no dev
tool (spec §11 TU-3). Each Show Me edit is an ordinary undo step, and
exiting a tutorial undoes nothing. Show Me does three jobs:

- it helps a person who is stuck;
- it lets a proof run every tutorial to the end with no person present;
- it is what auto-play will use for the videos (§8).

## 5. What stays out of the model phase

- Rolling tutorials out to every guide page, and the worked examples each
  page still lacks (after TU4, one batch per page).
- Auto-play and video capture (§8).
- The `framejob://` link (#385).

## 5a. The practice project (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now)

A small project bundled with the app, made so that every model tutorial's
`needs` are met in it, and kept so as the set grows. Built in TU1b, spec §11
TU-7.

- **What it holds:** at least two clips with sound that meet on one track
  (Split, Volume, Cross-dissolve), room above them for a title (Add a title),
  and enough length to set an in/out range and export it (Export a range).
- **Its media is made, not found:** generated by a script checked in beside
  it, so it carries no third-party footage or music and its provenance is
  written down (a `PROVENANCE.md`, as `app/Resources/Models/` has). A few
  megabytes at most; the product still has no ffmpeg dependency.
- **It is never written:** Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it
  as an untitled copy (its media copied or referenced read-only, so a save
  asks where), and a tutorial whose `needs` are unmet offers the same.
- **It is what the proof runs on** (§7) and what the videos will film (§8).

## 6. The model set

Five tutorials, chosen so that between them they use every step shape the
design has. If these five work, the remaining tutorials need content
only, not new machinery.

| # | Tutorial (guide page) | Steps | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Change a clip's volume** (`audio.md`) | select a clip with sound → Sound ▸ Volume opens → change the level → play | the owner's example: a selection wait, a sub-tab and section reveal, a value-changed wait |
| 2 | **Split a clip** (`editing.md`) | select a clip → move the playhead into it → Clip ▸ Split (⌘T) | a playhead wait (the person scrubs), a menu or key action, a count wait, `$created` |
| 3 | **Add a title** (`canvas-and-layers.md`) | press T or the bar's Add Text → type the words in Text ▸ Content → drag it on the canvas | a bar-button spotlight, a new clip the next step follows, text entry while the panel is up, a canvas gesture (`changed: video.position`) |
| 4 | **Cross-dissolve two clips** (`motion-and-transitions.md`) | select the later of two clips that meet → Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve → set its length in the Transition section | `needs` that the project may not meet, a submenu item, a section that only exists once the edit has applied |
| 5 | **Export a range** (`export.md`) | set In and Out (I, O) → File ▸ Export… → pick a format in the sheet → Export | view-state waits (`range`), a sheet and spotlights inside it (the export sheet has no accessibility ids today), an outcome that is not an edit (`queued`) |

The owner kept these five (2026-10-31).

## 7. Verification

- **`make test`, no app:** `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` reads every
  guide page. It checks the following and fails on anything unknown, naming
  the page and step:
  - each tutorial's JSON against §4.2's vocabulary;
  - each `show_me` tool name and argument key against the build's catalog
    snapshot;
  - each `section:` id and target name against the names the app publishes;
  - each menu path a sentence names against
    `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`;
  - each `changed` path against the schema.
- **Over MCP:** dev tools `tutorial_start {id}`, `tutorial_state`,
  `tutorial_step {action: show_me|next|back|skip}` and
  `tutorial_exit`, compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`.
  `tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py` runs each model tutorial three ways:
  - **as a person:** it meets each wait with the ordinary tools
    (`set_selection`, `set_audio`, `set_playhead`, `perform_menu_item`, …)
    and reads that the runner advanced and that the inspector shows the
    revealed tab, sub-tab and section (`select_inspector_tab` with no tab);
  - **by Show Me alone:** it runs every step's Show Me to the end and reads
    the project back with `get_project`;
  - **with `needs` unmet:** on an empty project it reads the panel's
    sentence and its offer of the practice project.

  Both the person and Show Me runs start from the practice project.
- **Seeing it:** `snapshot_ui` learns the coach panel as a window kind; a
  capture of the editor with the spotlight up, in both looks.
- **`docs/manual-checks.md` rows:**
  - the ring sits on the right control and follows a window resize and an
    inspector scroll;
  - the panel never takes typing from a field;
  - a person completes each of the five by hand.

## 8. Videos (after TU4, recorded here so the format allows for them)

Every step that has a `show_me` can run unattended. Auto-play performs the
step, holds for a reading time based on the sentence's length, and moves on,
with the coach panel serving as the caption. The recorder (with Include
Frame Job windows) or `screencapture` films it. One question is left for
that phase: a tool call doesn't move the pointer, so a video may want Show
Me performed through the UI instead (the menu item, a synthesized click on
the control). The format doesn't need to change for that; only the
performer does.

## 9. Phases

Each phase is one litecode pipeline, gated and committed on its own on this
worktree's branch, `worktree-tutorial-handler`. The session is isolated from
the main checkout, so the merge into main is the owner's (or a session in the
main tree's) after the last phase.

- **TU0 — decisions and words.** Write
  `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`: TU-1 one source (the guide's
  list plus HTML-comment halves), TU-2 the closed vocabulary and its checker,
  TU-3 Show Me's tool form through `AgentServer.execute` with ordinary undo
  and its menu form the menu bar's own item, TU-4 the
  non-activating panel and the click-through spotlight window, TU-5 `needs`
  checked before step 1 and the practice project offered when they are not
  met, TU-6 the practice project: made media, opened as an untitled copy,
  never written. Add the index row and the `CONTEXT.md` terms (Tutorial,
  Practice project).
- **TU1 — the five as text, plus the checker.** Write the five tutorials
  into their pages; their sentences are useful to a reader before any app
  code exists. Also: the extractor, the bundle step, the app's target-name
  table, and `tutorial_check.py` in `make test`. The step vocabulary, settled
  here, is written down normatively in spec §11 TU-2.
- **TU1b — the practice project.** The generator script and its
  provenance, the bundled project and media, Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open
  Practice Project opening it as an untitled copy, and whatever an agent
  needs to open it too. Every model tutorial's `needs` met in it, checked.
- **TU2 — the runner, with no chrome.** The model, the condition evaluator,
  variables, reveal and Show Me, the dev tools, and `tutorial_proof.py`'s
  person and Show Me runs over the five.
- **TU3 — the chrome.** The coach panel, the spotlight, Help ▸
  Tutorials, the export sheet's ids, `snapshot_ui`'s panel kind, the
  `needs` run, the manual-checks rows, and the guide's page on tutorials
  plus its `menus-and-shortcuts.md` row.
- **TU4 — the owner's trial.** The owner runs the five. What they change is
  fixed here, and the decision whether to roll out (and in what order) is
  made here.

## 10. The owner's answers (2026-10-31)

1. **The model set:** keep the five in §6.
2. **Practice material:** build a bundled practice project now (§5a, TU1b).
3. **The word:** "Tutorials" (Help ▸ Tutorials), and tutorial in the code.

Build with litecode, one pipeline per phase, every phase back to back.

## Record

(Each phase's record goes here: what landed, what was measured, what the
review found, what is owed.)

### TU0 + TU1 (2026-10-31)

**Landed.** Spec §11 TU-1..TU-6 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`,
TU-2 holding the step vocabulary normatively (§4.2 above is its first draft),
TU-3 splitting Show Me into the tool form (`AgentServer.execute`) and the menu
form (the built menu bar's own item); the index rows; **Tutorial** and
**Practice project** in `CONTEXT.md`. The five model tutorials in their guide
pages (`audio.md` § Volume, `editing.md` § Splitting, `canvas-and-layers.md`
§ Text clips, `motion-and-transitions.md` after Add a transition, `export.md`
§ Range). `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` (the one parser) and the app
build's "Write Tutorials" step, which writes `Contents/Resources/Tutorials.json`;
`app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`, the spotlight target table, called only
by the probe so far; `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift` and
`tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`, with its fixtures and a
selftest; the gate's and `proof_app.py`'s inputs gain `docs/guide` and
`tools/tutorials`. No op, no `rc_*`, no format bump, no catalog change.

**Measured.** `tutorial_check: 5 tutorials, 17 steps, 0 problems`;
`tutorial_check --selftest: 15/15 passed` (CONTROL and 14 mutants, one per
refusal class); the probe built through `swift_build` in 29.4 s.
`make typecheck` 0 errors and the four baseline warnings. `make gate`'s first
run passed names, typecheck, fmt, lint and test (230 s) and failed app: the
"Write Tutorials" step's PATH puts `/usr/bin` first, and the extractor's
`str | None` annotations do not run on its Python 3.9.6; with `from __future__
import annotations` the extractor's output under `/usr/bin/python3` is
byte-identical to the default `python3`'s, and the second run passed (`gate:
PASS 79s`). The Release bundle's `Tutorials.json` is byte-identical to the
extractor's output (`cmp` exit 0).

**Review.** litecode's adversary raised three objections before the code,
all accepted: Add a title's Show Me now starts with `add_track` (the tool has
no new-track fallback, unlike T); `has_transition` joined the clip filter so
Cross-dissolve cannot stall on a pair already dissolved; TU-3 splits the tool
form from the menu form, since `perform_menu_item` is a dev tool. The review
passed with no blocker or should-fix and four nits in the extractor and the
checker (a refused tutorial comment counting its steps as outside a
tutorial; a `<!-- tutorial` inside a list item not refused; the selftest
folder misnamed in a docstring; a duplicate id reported at line 0), carried
into TU1b.

**Owed.** The four review nits (TU1b). The CLAUDE.md edits (the root map's
`tools/tutorials/` row and `make test` line, `app/CLAUDE.md`'s Tutorials
entry) were applied by the orchestrator with this commit.

### TU1b (2026-10-31)

**Landed.** Spec §11 TU-7, recorded before the code, and TU-2 (3)'s
definitions of `has_sound` and `has_pixels`. The practice project:
`tools/practice/` (`practice_media.swift` draws and encodes one scene with
AVFoundation, Core Graphics and Core Text; `practice_generator.swift` writes
the three, probes them with `MediaImporter.probeBlocking` and builds
`project.json` through the core's own ops; `make_practice.py` builds it through
`swift_build`, replaces the package and writes `SHA256SUMS`), the generated
`app/Resources/Practice/Practice Project.framejob` (Dawn, Sea, Night: three
6 s clips with 1 s handles back to back on Track 1, no transition) with its
`PROVENANCE.md`, bundled by `project.yml`. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice
Project (`AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift`, `PracticeProject.open()`: an untitled
copy titled "Practice Project") and its mirror `new_project {practice:
true}`; a saved copy carries its media into its own package
(`ProjectDocument+PracticeMedia.swift`'s `write(to:…)`, fed by the save
funnel in `+CacheSaves`), and Consolidate relinks a carried file rather than
copying it; an open of anything inside the app is a practice copy
(`ProjectDocumentController`) or a refusal (`open_project`).
`TutorialClipFacts.swift` answers the clip filter's five keys per clip;
`tutorial_probe.swift` reads the package as the app opens it and
`tutorial_check.py`'s `check_practice` holds every tutorial's `needs`, the
media and `SHA256SUMS` in `make test`. `practice_project_proof.py` over MCP.
TU1's four review nits fixed, each a selftest case where it is a refusal.
No op, no `rc_*`, no format bump, no new tool.

**Measured.** `make_practice.py`: the package is 1,497,141 bytes (Dawn.mov
438,263, Sea.mov 416,277, Night.mov 637,027, project.json 5,574; cap
4,000,000); ffmpeg's volumedetect on Sea.mov: max −14.9 dB.
`tutorial_check --selftest: 20/20 passed`; `tutorial_check: 5 tutorials,
17 steps, 0 problems`. `make typecheck` 0 errors and the four baseline
warnings. `make gate`: `gate: PASS 245s` (test 125 s, app 109 s). On Release:
`practice_project_proof.py` `scores: 10 pass, 0 fail of 10`;
`graphics_menu_proof.py` `44/44 checks passed`. Mutants: `followsClip`'s `<=`
as `<` and `hasTransition` inverted each failed `tutorial_check` (the cross
dissolve's `needs` unmet); the `openPracticeProject:` row dropped failed
`v2_menu.py` H2; `newProject` ignoring `practice` failed P1 (and P5); §F's
`write` returning after `super` failed P4 (no media carried, paths in the
bundle) and R1; `openProject`'s inside-the-app refusal removed failed O1, and
N1 caught the reopened bundle's `cache/` written into the Debug app. The

# Tutorials — road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: in progress. The owner's answers (2026-10-31) are in §10; TU0
records the decisions in spec §11.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model tutorials** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Tutorials are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The tutorial dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Tutorials get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Tutorial**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project or
the practice project. It is the word in the menu (Help ▸ Tutorials) and in
the code. The word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: walkthrough,
wizard (which suggests the app makes the choices), lesson.

**Practice project**: a small project bundled with the app, with media made
for the tutorials, that Help ▸ Tutorials opens as an untitled copy so the
bundled one is never written (§5a).

**Step**: one numbered item in a tutorial. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
Me does.

## 4. The shape

### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list

A tutorial is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Tutorial:`
heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

```markdown
### Tutorial: change a clip's volume
<!-- tutorial {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
```

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every tutorial into one `Tutorials.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

### 4.2 The step vocabulary

**The normative text is spec §11 TU-2** (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`); this
section is the first draft. TU1 added `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a
menu form of Show Me, `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the
filter's `follows_clip` and `has_transition`.

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.
Every key is optional except that a step has a sentence.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the tutorial does not require this step. |

Variables: `$selection` (the clip ids when the step began), `$created`
(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip
in time order that matches, for a Show Me that has to choose a clip).

### 4.3 The runner and the coach panel

- **The coach panel.** A small non-activating floating panel beside the
  editor window, the same kind of panel as the recorder. It shows the title,
  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.
- **The spotlight.** A borderless, click-through child window over the
  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when
  the layout moves. Because it is a window, it sits above the Metal and
  `AVPlayerLayer` layers.
- **Needs.** Before step 1, the tutorial's `needs` are checked against the
  open project. When they are not met, the panel says what is missing and
  how to get it, and offers the practice project (§5a), for example "This
  tutorial needs a clip with sound. Open the practice project, or open a
  movie of your own (File ▸ Open…)". It does not start until they are met.
- **Where to start one.** **Help ▸ Tutorials ▸** has one submenu per guide
  page, filled from `Tutorials.json`. A "Try it in Frame Job" link from
  the online guide (`framejob://tutorial/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

### 4.4 Show Me

Show Me's tool form (and each tool entry of a list) runs through
`AgentServer.execute`, the path the Assistant's calls take; its menu form
performs the built menu bar's own item, the path a click takes, with no dev
tool (spec §11 TU-3). Each Show Me edit is an ordinary undo step, and
exiting a tutorial undoes nothing. Show Me does three jobs:

- it helps a person who is stuck;
- it lets a proof run every tutorial to the end with no person present;
- it is what auto-play will use for the videos (§8).

## 5. What stays out of the model phase

- Rolling tutorials out to every guide page, and the worked examples each
  page still lacks (after TU4, one batch per page).
- Auto-play and video capture (§8).
- The `framejob://` link (#385).

## 5a. The practice project (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now)

A small project bundled with the app, made so that every model tutorial's
`needs` are met in it, and kept so as the set grows. Built in TU1b, spec §11
TU-7.

- **What it holds:** at least two clips with sound that meet on one track
  (Split, Volume, Cross-dissolve), room above them for a title (Add a title),
  and enough length to set an in/out range and export it (Export a range).
- **Its media is made, not found:** generated by a script checked in beside
  it, so it carries no third-party footage or music and its provenance is
  written down (a `PROVENANCE.md`, as `app/Resources/Models/` has). A few
  megabytes at most; the product still has no ffmpeg dependency.
- **It is never written:** Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it
  as an untitled copy (its media copied or referenced read-only, so a save
  asks where), and a tutorial whose `needs` are unmet offers the same.
- **It is what the proof runs on** (§7) and what the videos will film (§8).

## 6. The model set

Five tutorials, chosen so that between them they use every step shape the
design has. If these five work, the remaining tutorials need content
only, not new machinery.

| # | Tutorial (guide page) | Steps | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Change a clip's volume** (`audio.md`) | select a clip with sound → Sound ▸ Volume opens → change the level → play | the owner's example: a selection wait, a sub-tab and section reveal, a value-changed wait |
| 2 | **Split a clip** (`editing.md`) | select a clip → move the playhead into it → Clip ▸ Split (⌘T) | a playhead wait (the person scrubs), a menu or key action, a count wait, `$created` |
| 3 | **Add a title** (`canvas-and-layers.md`) | press T or the bar's Add Text → type the words in Text ▸ Content → drag it on the canvas | a bar-button spotlight, a new clip the next step follows, text entry while the panel is up, a canvas gesture (`changed: video.position`) |
| 4 | **Cross-dissolve two clips** (`motion-and-transitions.md`) | select the later of two clips that meet → Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve → set its length in the Transition section | `needs` that the project may not meet, a submenu item, a section that only exists once the edit has applied |
| 5 | **Export a range** (`export.md`) | set In and Out (I, O) → File ▸ Export… → pick a format in the sheet → Export | view-state waits (`range`), a sheet and spotlights inside it (the export sheet has no accessibility ids today), an outcome that is not an edit (`queued`) |

The owner kept these five (2026-10-31).

## 7. Verification

- **`make test`, no app:** `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` reads every
  guide page. It checks the following and fails on anything unknown, naming
  the page and step:
  - each tutorial's JSON against §4.2's vocabulary;
  - each `show_me` tool name and argument key against the build's catalog
    snapshot;

s=s.rstrip("\n")+"\n"+"""- **TU-8 — The model and the runner: `Tutorials.json` read into typed tutorials, one runner
  per editor window, event-driven, no chrome.**
  1. *The model* (`TutorialModel.swift`) decodes format 1 and refuses, per tutorial and with
     its reason, any key, type or value outside TU-2 (2)–(9): closed keys at every level, the
     id pattern, the filter's keys and kinds, `min`/`max`, `range` exactly one of its two
     forms, `sheet` `"export"`, the `true` literals, a `reveal` against `InspectorTab`,
     `ClipSubTab` and the section's home in `TutorialTargets.sections`, a `spotlight`
     against `TutorialTargets`, the Show Me shapes, and every `$`-string and `$`-key. A
     refused tutorial cannot be started; the rest of the file still reads. The catalog,
     menu-bar, inventory and fixture-path checks stay the checker's, at build time; one
     failing at run time is a refused Show Me. `tutorial_check.py` holds the model to the
     checker both ways through its probe: every tutorial the checker accepts decodes, and
     each model mutant is refused.
  2. *Start.* At most one runner per editor window (`EditorViewController.tutorialRunner`);
     starting one replaces it; Exit drops it and undoes nothing; closing the window ends
     it. A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the window's edited project with
     `TutorialClipFacts`, and when no clip meets them the start is refused in one sentence:
     `This tutorial needs ` + `a clip` (or `a`/`an` `<kind> clip`) + (nothing, or ` that `
     + the predicates) + `.`, the predicates in `TutorialClipFacts.keys` order — `has
     sound`/`has no sound`, `has a picture`/`has no picture`, `meets the clip before it on
     its track`/`does not meet the clip before it on its track`, `has a transition
     in`/`has no transition in` — joined `p`, `p1 and p2`, `p1, p2 and p3`.
  3. *Triggers, no polling.* A committed document change or a view-state change (the
     editor's `projectDocumentDidChange`; a live tick ignored), a playhead move, a rate
     change, the editor window's sheet attaching or ending, an export started (the sheet's
     Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool), and a forward step entry (start, Next,
     Skip, an advance by a met wait). The inspector tab is not one. Each trigger schedules
     ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn, so the event that met a wait has
     finished first. A step entered by Back schedules none, so Back stays where it lands
     until a later trigger. A step with no `wait` never advances by evaluation. While a Show
     Me runs, evaluations are held, entry ones included, and one runs after its last
     entry. A wait met on forward entry cascades: the next step's entry schedules its own.
  4. *Conditions.* Each step's baseline is taken as it begins: the selection, the set of
     clip ids, the range, and the latches cleared. `selection` holds when the count is in
     [min, max] and every selected clip matches; `changed` when any clip selected at the
     start differs at any listed path from its start value (the edited project's clip JSON,
     a dotted path, absent read as null); `clips` when at least `added` ids are new since the
     start (of `kind`); `playhead` when it is strictly inside any clip of the set; `range
     set` when a range exists, `changed` when that edge differs from its start; `sheet` when
     the window's attached sheet is the export sheet; `export_started` and `playing` when
     latched since the step began. Every condition must hold; a met wait advances in that
     evaluation.
  5. *Variables* resolve per TU-2 (9) at each Show Me call: `$selection` is the step's start
     selection; `$created` the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier call of this
     Show Me, that added any (recorded per step begin, so Back restores it); time order is by
     start, ties front track first; `$time`'s span is the earliest start to the latest end,
     `middle` snapped to the frame; `$track` is the front track when the call is made.
  6. *Navigation and reveal.* A step begins with its baseline, then its `reveal` through the
     inspector's own paths — the tab, the sub-tab when the selection offers it, the target
     section opened by `InspectorSection.reveal()` (which writes no preference), then

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  waits holding an unfinished entry, so `take`'s wait always ends.

  compositor `reach`es each frame it asks for, and the workers skip past it;

  push out the frames drawn ahead. A pass's end line (`done`, `full`,
  `stopped`) is written at its stop. `Slot` lives at the foot of
  `LayerRenderersGraphic.swift` (a pure move under the cap); at 600 lines
  the file's next cut is the background branches.

  Subtitles as one enum: the PostScript face, `case`, size (of

  presets and is not edited by a look.
- `FillerWords.swift` — THE filler vocabulary (spec §11 TR-8): the set,
  `normalized` (lowercased, punctuation and whitespace trimmed both ends),
  `isFiller`, and `MediaTranscript.captionWords(for:in:)`, `words(for:in:)`

  disfluent transcript captions as before.

  transcript when its marker serves `.captions` (`cloudWords`); otherwise the

  network. The handler's first line reads

  window plus `recognitionPadSeconds` each side (`recognitionJob`).
- `DeviceTranscriptCache.swift` — `get_transcript`'s own cache of what the
  on-device recogniser heard (spec §11 TR-14): one file per media and
  language in the package's `cache/device-transcripts/`, keyed by the

  from a stored run that contains the call's span, else recognises and
  stores (dropping runs the new one contains), never after a cancel or a
  file change during the run; written through `CacheLedger`. Captions,
  the filler tools and the cloud readers never read it.
- `CaptionPages.swift` — word-caption PAGES (spec §11 W-7), pure and
  synchronous so it runs on whichever engine thread calls it:

  clip's last frame), the pager (speaker, 0.25 s gap, sentence mark,

  page timing that abuts under `breakGap` and never passes the span.

  `NSMenuItem`s carrying `representedObject`, because `addItem(withTitle:)`

  land, and promises nothing about the next run.

  the id still owed a delete.

  no retry of the POST or requests by any unrelated id.

  `AssemblyAIConfiguration` is the ONE reader of `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` and

  the one argument-domain reader, which `AssistantConfiguration` and
  `DevAssistantLaunch` reuse), and the ONE line

  directory `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` makes, `0700` at each level it makes

  a code AssemblyAI refuses comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence.
- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its
  `.complete.json` sidecar (`MediaImporter.transcriptsKind` is the post kind,

  `JSONValueRange`, and neither ever re-serialises — a `0.98` does not
  survive that. Both `File` inits throw on a `words` that is not an array, so
  `read` answers nil and `isCurrent` false rather than caching zero words;
  `isCurrent` asks `serves(_:for: .captions)`.
  THE MAPPING is here: a word is a clip's when `in ≤ start × 600 <
  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped
  through `Transcriber.placed` (R6-10). That `× 600` goes through
  `sourceTicks(milliseconds:)`, the one integer multiply on the caption
  path, clamped in `Int` to ±`Ticks.max / 600` first and deliberately NOT to

  `undeleted(in:)` is the janitor's.

  at a time, in arrival order, through the `Gate` actor; `releaseNow` is the

  queues its release, so a stalled gate cannot hold a finished run hostage.
- `Transcriber.swift` (+`Languages`, +`Extract`, +`Jobs`) ·
  `TranscribeSheetController.swift` (+`Cloud`: the AssemblyAI half — the

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and

  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a

  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never

  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at

  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.
  `GraphicStore+History.swift` is the kept revisions and the rename journal
  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'
  mean a DELETED module. `GraphicStore+Import.swift`'s `importAsset` files a name
  `asset(name)` cannot use under `GraphicAssetName.legalized`, a renamed
  copy taking `-2`, `-3`, … while `holdsAsset(named:)` (scan or disk) says
  the name is held, and answers `name`/`renamedFrom` (G-23 (c), (d)).
  `landNew` is the `.fjgraphic` import's write (G-47 (e)): bytes landed
  under a name not yet taken, never replacing a file. **`drain()` is not
  re-entrant: never call `rescan()` from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer.**
  `stop()` bumps a generation under `queue.sync`. `makeLibrary()` is a NEW
  builder every call (a library freezes on first use). It also writes the
  app's bundled reference into an EXISTING folder as `API.md` and `API.d.ts`
  (`writeManual()`, from `start()` for a saved package, `ensureFolder()` and
  `write()`; only when the bytes differ) — never a reason to create the
  folder (G-14).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

- `CaptionImporter.swift` (SubRip grammar) · `CaptionExporter.swift` (`.srt` /
  `.vtt` from one all-text track, never guessed; a popup built from
  `NSMenuItem`s carrying `representedObject`, because `addItem(withTitle:)`
  REMOVES a same-titled row).
- `CloudTranscriber.swift` (+`Report`, +`Media`) — `TranscriptionEngine` (`apple` |
  `assemblyai`, persisted under `FrameJobCaptionEngine`) and the cloud engine
  over the SAME `Transcriber.Job` / `Outcome` / `CancelToken`. `run` is its
  serial queue and the main-thread completion; `transcribe` is the
  synchronous body — the janitor FIRST, the jobs grouped by MEDIA, each
  media classified cached / HELD / to upload, then each job's words cut out
  of its media's one transcript, through `captionWords` (fillers out,
  TR-1); the keyless admission asks `serves(.captions)`. `+Report` holds what the `Outcome` has no
  room for (`uploaded` with the transcript-write and marker-write results,
  `transcriptWritten` and `stampWritten`, `cached`,
  `janitorDeleted`, `janitorFailed`, `janitorDeferred`, `held`, and

  `billedSeconds` is the ONE sum of `audioSeconds` — each term floored at 0,
  saturating at `Int.max` — that the bill sentence and `audio_seconds` read;
  `cacheWarnings` is one sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not
  land, and promises nothing about the next run.
  A nil client admits only a nonempty, entirely
  current batch and skips janitor/network, retaining pending IDs as deferred.

  every exit, the server's model and language filtered through
  `withoutCredential` and then bounded at 64 Unicode scalars (`bounded`,

  whose served strings — every key and value at any depth, scanned from the
  bytes (`TranscriptWord.servedStrings`, R6-23) — repeat the key refused

  written before its marker, and the DELETE last with its answer recorded —
  its `remote_deleted` rewrite only over a first write that landed (#187).
  Spec §11's R6-11: a media in this run's
  `janitorFailed` is never fetched, since its cache file is the one record of
  the id still owed a delete.
- `CloudEstimate.swift` — what a cloud run would COST and why, PURE: a
  `Fate` per media (`upload(Reason)` / `cached` / `awaitingDelete(Reason)` /

  cost if the delete clears. `facts(jobs:media:cacheDirectory:)` is the ONE
  member that opens a file, so a sheet can recompute the readout per

- `CloudProgress.swift` — the cloud run's one number and the words beside it,

  147× and holding, and the five detail lines, a count under a megabyte spelt
  `<1`. The run publishes
  `max(previous, computed)`.
- `AssemblyAITranscript.swift` — the wire VALUES, and
  `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the ONE spelling of the vocabulary's
  trim/de-duplicate/cap that the sheet's field and the tool's argument share:
  `TranscriptOptions`,
  `TranscriptRequest` (whose `encode` is the whole wire body — `language_code`

  `.fillers` also needs the marker's own `disfluencies` true.

  put on the wire. `delete(id:cancel:)` reads the run's token as a STOP and
  never attaches it: a DELETE is cut `deleteAfterStop` (2 s) of wall clock

  like any other (R6-19); `send`'s `stop`/`grace` and `+Session`'s

  `SecretStore.swift` — WHERE the client speaks and WHAT it says it is.
  `AssemblyAIConfiguration` is the ONE reader of `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` and
  `-RCSecretFolder`, both out of the ARGUMENT domain only (its `argument` is
  the one argument-domain reader, which `AssistantConfiguration` and

  in the feature that names `AppSupport.directory` (spec §11's R6-9: with an
  endpoint set and no secret folder, `store()` answers an EMPTY `MemoryStore`

  `assemblyai-key` by default, `anthropic-key` for the assistant's key
  (AI-8, AI-13, whose `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` plays R6-9's endpoint). Non-`https` is accepted only for

  directory `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` makes, `0700` at each level it makes

  the probe's. The language table is a DATED static list, not an authority:
  a code AssemblyAI refuses comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence.
- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its
  `.complete.json` sidecar (`MediaImporter.transcriptsKind` is the post kind,

  in after a `.sortedKeys` header, `init(data:)` cuts it back out with

  survive that. Both `File` inits throw on a `words` that is not an array, so
  `read` answers nil and `isCurrent` false rather than caching zero words;
  `isCurrent` asks `serves(_:for: .captions)`.
  THE MAPPING is here: a word is a clip's when `in ≤ start × 600 <
  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped
  through `Transcriber.placed` (R6-10). That `× 600` goes through
  `sourceTicks(milliseconds:)`, the one integer multiply on the caption
  path, clamped in `Int` to ±`Ticks.max / 600` first and deliberately NOT to
  `maxSourceTicks` (R6-10's extension). A RAMPED clip's job carries

  calls it. **Never `Task {}` here** — a main-thread caller's actor would be
  inherited and the semaphore would deadlock. `Handle` is what
  `CancelToken` holds for a running analysis. Two host facts it is built on
  (road map 8 §10.6): `status(forModules:)` is `.installed` only for a

- `Transcriber.swift` (+`Languages`, +`Extract`, +`Jobs`) ·

  Language popup's second population, `RunRequest` (the ONE function from

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
